**Derivation:** The $N$-th rational solution of the massive Thirring model is built from a Jordan chain of length $N$ at an embedded eigenvalue, yielding a double-Wronskian denominator that is a polynomial of degree $2N$ in $x$ (with coefficients depending on $t$). For large $|t|$, this polynomial factorizes into $N$ quadratic factors, each describing one of the $N$ constituent algebraic solitons centered near the $N$ real roots of the leading-order polynomial. Each quadratic factor has exactly one simple zero in the upper half-plane and one in the lower half-plane (the two are conjugate-related under the model's reduction). Because the $N$ leading-order roots are real and distinct, the $N$ upper-half-plane poles remain separated and do not coalesce. Hence the total number of poles in $\operatorname{Im}x>0$ equals $N$.
